overview: This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to study whether it should use distributed ledger technology, a shared, tamper-resistant digital record system (blockchain is the best-known type), in handling veterans' benefits. The study would look at whether recording key steps of claims decisions this way could make the process more traceable and reliable, reduce fraudulent or inaccurate claims, and help spot problems in benefit payments, along with the risks. The VA would consult technology experts, veterans service organizations and other federal agencies, and report its findings and any recommended pilot programs to Congress within one year. As of October 10, 2025, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say a careful study is a low-cost way to learn whether newer technology could make veterans' claims more secure and transparent before the VA commits money to it.
against: Critics say the VA already struggles with major technology upgrades, and that a study of an unproven technology could pull attention from fixing existing systems that veterans rely on.
